trigger_input.complaint: Installed two days ago, still no connection

signals.threshold: An active customer line must have held sessions; normal baseline is 2-3 sessions per day

signals.value: download=0 MB/day and upload=0 MB/day for all 7 days; monthly averages=0 MB
signals.threshold: An active served line should show nonzero customer traffic
Strong/normal optical power is above -25 dBm; value is within band
Normal TX power is 0 to +5 dBm; value is within band

detection.summary: The active newly installed line has normal optical readings but has never established a session and has zero traffic, confirming a single-customer service fault.

diagnosis.root_cause: The ONU is online and authenticated with healthy optical readings, and its RADIUS entry exists and is CRM-consistent, but the customer VLAN is still 46 instead of the expected 1116. VLAN 46 is the factory-default, never-provisioned VLAN, explaining the absence of sessions and traffic.
evidence: Live ONU query shows responds=true, online=1, auth_flag=Auth, and exchange=Finish.
Live RX power is -18.95 dBm and TX power is 2.51 dBm, both healthy.
OLT ping, SNMP, and OID subtree queries all succeed, ruling out an OLT failure.
All observed peer ONUs on EPON0/6 are online, so there is no shared port or splitter outage.
RADIUS entry exists, is CRM-consistent, and has no mismatches.
The line has zero sessions in 24 hours and seven days and zero traffic.
The expected customer VLAN is 1116, but the actual VLAN is 46; VLAN 46 is the factory-default unprovisioned VLAN.
Optical history is stable: RX change -0.13 dBm, TX change -0.04 dBm, distance unchanged at 52, and TX bias remains within the healthy range.

remediation.reason: The ONU is online, authenticated, optically healthy, and has a valid CRM-consistent RADIUS entry, but remains on factory-default VLAN 46 instead of the expected customer VLAN 1116. This is a stuck provisioning condition, not an optical, RADIUS, OLT, or infrastructure failure.
remediation.instructions: Trigger ACS provisioning for lineid 4C:46:D1:09:7C:78 to apply customer VLAN 1116. Verify afterward that the ONU leaves VLAN 46, establishes a session, and passes traffic.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The ONU is online and responsive with healthy optical readings; resetting will not correct the missing VLAN provisioning.
The RADIUS entry already exists and is consistent with CRM.
Optical levels, distance, and history are stable, with no evidence of fibre or splitter degradation.
OLT connectivity is healthy and peer ONUs on the PON are online, ruling out a shared infrastructure failure.

escalation.summary: A single newly installed customer line is out of service despite healthy optical levels, ONU authentication, OLT connectivity, and a valid CRM-consistent RADIUS entry. The ONU remains on factory-default VLAN 46 instead of the expected customer VLAN 1116, causing no sessions and zero traffic. Trigger ACS provisioning for line 4C:46:D1:09:7C:78, then verify that it leaves VLAN 46, establishes a session, and passes traffic.

ground_truth.root_cause: The CPE is still on VLAN 46, the factory-default management VLAN it ships with. The TR-069 provisioning step that migrates it to VLAN 1999 and its data VLAN never completed, so the device is registered on the fibre but has no path onto the network.
expected_reasoning: The ONU is online with RX -18.92 and TX 2.50, both excellent
The live probe confirms the ONU and its peers are responding normally
The OLT and router are healthy, so the physical layer works end to end
Despite that, the customer has zero sessions and zero traffic since installation
A radcheck row does exist for this CPE MAC, so this is not a missing RADIUS entry
The VLAN walk shows the customer on VLAN 46 where VLAN 1116 is expected
VLAN 46 is the factory-default management VLAN a CPE ships with
Provisioning should have migrated it to 1999 and the port's data VLAN, and did not
The device is present on the fibre and has no path onto the network
distractors: Zero sessions with a healthy physical layer is also the RADIUS missing-entry signature
Excellent optical readings invite a no_fault conclusion on the network side
The VLAN walk is not an obvious first move
